name: Popstar
lede: Popstar is a dusty, rose-tinted red, a name recorded by web color lists with no older dictionary source and no documented coiner.

sections.title: A web color list name, origin undocumented
sections.body:
ColorHub's library carries Popstar from a general web color-name list, which cites no original source, pigment maker or standards body for it [1]. None of the books consulted here, including Ridgway's 1912 plates and the ISCC-NBS 1955 filings, record this name, and no earlier print source for it turned up [1]. Who coined it, and when, is undocumented in the sources available here.

Its closest look-alikes on file are [[carmine-red|Carmine Red]], almost the same color, and [[brick-red|Brick Red]], more vivid, with [[reddish-crimson|Reddish Crimson]] close behind, also more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds a match for this rose-red in only 9 of them, about 0.04 percent, rarer than 69 percent of our named colors [3]. Its most common role inside a painting, when it does appear, is as an accent, present in all 9 cases, ranked by lightness rather than raw area [3].

The earliest dated match is a 1571 portrait by François Clouet; our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and the data is too sparse here for a reliable century trend [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
